Triage first-touch (triage seat, daily round 2026-08-27, session `session_01Czs5tCwMymUvzB9QCA2yhH`): graded **`pm:queue`**, type **Task**, routed `domain:spec` — the fix is the `IPubSub` contract docblock in `packages/spec/src/contracts/cluster-service.ts`, spec-lane sole-owner surface (describe/JSDoc prose face). Grading adopts the card's suggested shape: state the shipped guarantee honestly (at-most-once; a missed message is expected; handlers must be idempotent AND tolerate loss) and point at `deliverySemantics` for the per-channel declaration — prefer the driver-relative phrasing ("whatever the driver declares; no shipped driver exceeds at-most-once") so a future durable driver lands without rewriting the contract. Prose-only: no accept/reject behaviour changes, so no Clause-② tier. ⛔ The stronger designs the card names (type-readable per-driver guarantees, boot refusal of an `at-least-once` channel declaration) are out of scope — if measurement pulls toward them, that comes back as a decision card. The subscriber sweep stays un-carded per the card's own scoping; the two production consumers are cache-invalidation hints, the documented-acceptable class.

Premise re-checked at claim (origin/main `f75a38af`): the wrong sentence still at `cluster-service.ts:73` ("At-least-once delivery"); the measured correction still at `cluster.mdx:147` ("No shipped driver provides this yet"). Triage's adopted shape governs: state the shipped guarantee honestly — driver-relative phrasing ("whatever the driver declares; no shipped driver exceeds at-most-once"), handlers idempotent AND loss-tolerant, pointer to `deliverySemantics`; the stronger designs stay out of scope.
